reviewer: Claude Code (AI assistant). Not an independent human review.
method: A sweep of every page of the year for passages shared word for word by 4 or more papers that no counted opening of round one explains; each passage read, looked up in the year's lists and counted by its own opening words against every page in both transcriptions, by the thin-year rule (Y-THIN as amended on 23 November 2026: items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted; single paragraphs from runs of news counted by their own words, C-09); the items printed by every surviving paper admitted at the owner's word of 25 November 2026; scan checks of each admitted passage
scan_scope: Each crop covers the excerpt, the opening of the printed item. Long documents were not proofread in full.

new_groups.label: Cambridge, 3 August 1775: 'Last Monday morning, near Charlestown Neck, a warm fire began between our advanced parties and those of the enemy'
new_groups.definition: Printings of a paragraph of the news from the camp at Cambridge of 3 August 1775: 'Last Monday morning, near Charlestown Neck, a warm fire began between our advanced parties and those of the enemy, attended with cannonading from the enemy's works on Bunker-Hill. We took two marines prisoners, and killed several of the regulars ...'. A report from the American camp, as the papers printed it; most print it in a run of the camp's news without the dateline.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1775 printings, checked against the scan (round two: printed by every paper that survives for its weeks, found by the sweep check of 24-25 November 2026 and admitted at the owner's word).

dispositions_summary.method: Round two of 1775. The sweep check of 24 and 25 November 2026 (X-THIN-SWEEP; outputs/story_discovery_1779/sweep_check_25nov.md) read every passage of the 1775 pages shared word for word by 4 or more papers that no counted opening of round one explains, looked each up in the year's lists and counted it by its own opening words against every page of the year in both transcriptions. It found one item printed by every paper that survives for its weeks, which round one's lists did not name; asked, the owner chose on 25 November 2026 to admit it as the rule reads. Every printing was checked against its page scan by AI reviewers (scan_batches/round2.json, SCAN_PROTOCOL.md; verdicts in scan_verdicts/round2*.json).
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: As in round one (Y-THIN as amended, B1): an item printed by every newspaper that survives for its weeks is admitted. The Cambridge paragraph of 3 August is printed by all 6 papers of its weeks.

counted_item_by_item.The Cambridge report of the firing near: 6 of the 6 papers that survive for its weeks (CC 7 August, NHG 8 August, PP and NYG 14 August, VGDH 26 August, VGP 1 September), counted by its own words; only the Pennsylvania Packet prints the dateline 'CAMBRIDGE, August 3.', the others print the paragraph in a run of the camp's news.
